 Order

% 15.02.2023 Mr. A. Maitri, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that the essential grievance of the petitioner canvassed by way of the present petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India read with section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure 1973 ('Cr.P.C.'), is that despite the lapse of about 06 months, during which period no conciliation has been possible,
the CAW Cell/respondent No.2 has failed to register an FIR against the private respondents inter-alia under section 498A of the Indian Penal Code 1860 ('IPC').

2. Mr. Saransh, learned counsel appearing on behalf of Ms. Nandita Rao, learned ASC for respondents Nos.1 and 2, on instructions from the Inquiry Officer at the CAW Cell who is present,
submits that the conciliation process has been going-on since 14.10.2022 and the next date for the purpose is 17.02.2023.
Counsel for respondents Nos. 1 and 2 submits however, that if the petitioner takes the position that she is not interested in conciliation any further, an FIR can be registered.

Counsel points-out however, that the petitioner has not availed the remedy available under section 156(3) Cr.P.C. as mandated by the Supreme Court in Sakiri Vasu vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and Others 1 and has instead rushed to this court in its extraordinary jurisdiction.
3.

4. Pending applications, if any, stand disposed-of.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Be that as it may, without delving further into the matter, and in view of the statement made on behalf of the petitioner that she is no longer interested in attempting conciliation, the present petition is disposed- of, taking on record the statement of the Inquiry Officer that the CAW Cell will register an FIR promptly, in accordance with law.
4. Pending applications, if any, stand disposed-of.
